T: Pick your feet, grab a slice.
D: Two hard-nosed New York narcotics cops chase a French smuggling ring.
P: Serve the steak frites when Charnier sits down to dinner while Popeye freezes outside with his pizza.
S: Popeye eating a slice in the cold while Charnier dines in style across the road

Crisp-bottomed tray pizza with tomato, mozzarella, oregano and chilli, cut into slices you can eat standing up in the street. Press 500g pizza dough into an oiled 30 x 40cm tray and rest 20 minutes. Mix 200g passata with 1 crushed garlic clove, 1 tsp dried oregano and salt and spread over the dough. Top with 250g grated mozzarella and 20g grated parmesan. Bake at 240C for 15 minutes until the base is crisp and the cheese is browned. Finish with chilli flakes and cut into 12 slices.
the fancy meal across the road
Sear chicken livers pink in butter, flame with cognac, blitz with butter, thyme and shallot, set under clarified butter. Cornichons and warm baguette.
Cake doughnuts tossed in cinnamon sugar with drip coffee in paper cups, eaten in the car.
M: the meal Popeye watches through the window
Sirloin seared hard and rested, béarnaise (tarragon reduction, yolks, warm clarified butter) and hand-cut frites fried twice.
Charnier's home port of Marseille, where the film opens

Firm white fish, prawns and mussels in a saffron, fennel and tomato broth, with toasted baguette and garlicky rouille. Soften 1 sliced onion, 1 sliced fennel bulb and 3 garlic cloves in 3 tbsp olive oil for 10 minutes. Add a pinch of saffron, 400g tinned tomatoes, 1 litre fish stock and a strip of orange peel, and simmer 20 minutes. Add 500g firm white fish chunks for 4 minutes, then 12 green prawns and 500g mussels, covered, for 3 minutes until open. Mix 100g mayonnaise with 1 crushed garlic clove and a pinch each of saffron and cayenne. Serve with toasted baguette.
W: the French dessert across the street
Caramel set into ramekins, vanilla custard of 4 eggs, 2 yolks and 500ml milk poured over, baked in a water bath at 150C for 40 minutes, chilled and turned out.
K: a taste of Charnier's Marseille, where the heroin deal begins

Aniseed pastis with almond orgeat syrup and ice-cold water, turning cloudy and pale in a tall glass of ice. Put 30ml pastis and 15ml orgeat syrup into each of 4 tall glasses. Add 3 ice cubes, then slowly pour in 150ml chilled water and watch it turn cloudy. Stir once. Serve with a jug of cold water on the side so everyone can adjust the strength.

Add the cognac and flame it off carefully.
Blitz the livers, shallot and thyme with soft butter until smooth, then pack into a dish.
Pour melted butter over the top and chill until set.
Serve with cornichons and warm baguette.

dishes.make_ahead: Sauce best made just before serving

steps.text: Reduce the vinegar with tarragon and shallot until almost dry. Cut the potatoes into chips and dry them.
Fry the chips in the oil at 140C, then drain.
Whisk the yolks with the reduction over low heat until thick, then drizzle in the warm butter to make the sauce.
Season the steaks with salt and pepper, sear hard, then rest.
Fry the chips again until crisp and serve with the steaks and sauce.

veg.make_ahead: Sauce best made just before serving

steps.text: Reduce the vinegar with half the tarragon and the chopped shallot until almost dry. Cut the potatoes into chips and dry them.
Fry the chips in the vegetable oil at 140C, then drain.
Whisk the yolks with the strained reduction over low heat until thick, then drizzle in the warm butter and stir through the rest of the tarragon, chopped.
Brush the mushrooms with the olive oil and garlic, season with salt and pepper and sear in a hot heavy pan, pressed under a weight, for 5 minutes a side until tender.
Fry the chips again until crisp and serve with the mushrooms and sauce.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the day before, keep chilled

steps.text: Melt part of the sugar to an amber caramel and pour into 4 ramekins.
Whisk the eggs and yolks with the remaining sugar, milk and the seeds of the vanilla bean, then pour over the caramel.
Bake in a water bath at 150C until just set.
Chill overnight, then run a knife around the edge and turn out.
Put pastis and orgeat in each of 4 tall glasses, add ice, then pour in chilled water slowly and watch it cloud. Stir once and serve a jug of cold water on the side.

af.make_ahead: Anise tea up to 2 days ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Pour the boiling water over the star anise and fennel seeds, steep for 10 minutes and strain.
Chill the anise tea until cold.
Put anise tea and orgeat in each of 4 tall glasses, add ice, then pour in chilled water slowly so the orgeat clouds it. Stir once and serve a jug of cold water on the side.

s.note: the fancy meal across the road
s.how: Sear 400g trimmed chicken livers in butter until just pink. Flame with 2 tbsp cognac. Blitz with 150g soft butter, thyme and a sautéed shallot. Set in a dish under 50g melted butter for 4 hours. Serve with cornichons and warm baguette.

Warm 8 cake doughnuts in a 160C oven for 5 minutes. Toss in 100g caster sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon. Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water and pour into paper cups. Eat them hunched in front of the telly.

m.note: the meal Popeye watches through the window
m.how: Reduce 60ml white wine vinegar with tarragon and a shallot to 2 tbsp. Whisk with 3 yolks over a low heat, then drizzle in 200g warm clarified butter. Fry 1kg potato chips twice. Sear 4 sirloins hard, rest 5 minutes and serve.

w.note: the French dessert across the street
w.how: Melt 150g sugar to an amber caramel and pour into 4 ramekins. Whisk 4 eggs, 2 yolks, 100g sugar, 500ml milk and the seeds of a vanilla bean. Pour over, bake in a water bath at 150C for 40 minutes, chill overnight and turn out.
